messages:
Maya: Fathom Labs (customer) hit a midday surge on Dedicated; they're seeing sustained 429s and long tail latency. CS opened a sev2. Autoscaler log shows probes firing but new pods not Ready for ~3m. Can @Raj or @Liam triage?
Raj: Looking. Any repro steps or timestamps from the customer?
Maya: CS gave a short repro: ramp traffic to 120rps over 60s, observe ~30% 429 at peak. They attached a request_id and some controller logs.
Maya: snippet from customer's API errors:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 status=429 backend=dedicated-us-west
2026-03-18T14:02:15Z ERROR request_id=abcd2267 status=429 queue_len=12
```
Liam: I pulled our autoscaler logs for that window. I see probe timeouts and many imagePullBackOff retries around the same time. Not sure if it's registry throttle or scheduling.
Raj: Can you paste the autoscaler probe lines?
Liam: sure:
```
2026-03-18T14:02:03Z probe: tenant=fathom target=dedicated-pt-3 action=scale-up reason=queueing
2026-03-18T14:02:05Z pod-create start id=pod-zz1 imagepull=retries=1
2026-03-18T14:03:12Z pod-create failed id=pod-zz1 reason=ImagePullBackOff
2026-03-18T14:04:01Z probe: tenant=fathom target=dedicated-pt-3 action=scale-up reason=queueing
```
Ava: CS also mentioned a recent customer billing hold that briefly blocked image pull credentials rotation for that account earlier today. Could be related.
Raj: aha — if image pull creds rotated and were temporarily invalid, kube will keep retrying and that delays pods becoming Ready. Combine that with minReplicas low and probe holdoff, scaling appears slow.
Maya: CS says the billing hold was resolved at 14:01Z. But we still see 3+ minutes of lag after that.
Liam: two hypotheses: 1) registry throttling + backoff made pulls slower even after creds fixed; 2) autoscaler backoff/hysteresis prevented aggressive immediate spin-up because recent failed attempts triggered a hold.
Raj: I see autoscaler backoff entries at 14:02:30: "scaleback: tenant=fathom reason=recent-failures backoff=90s". That matches the stall window.
Maya: Customer impact: sustained 429s for ~3m while traffic spike continued. They want mitigation and a clear repro.
Raj: Immediate mitigation suggestions: - temporarily bump minReplicas for the tenant (we can do short window) - clear backoff for tenant so scaler can try again - pre-pull images into warm pool for that tenant if possible
Ava: I can coordinate CS to ask customer to up minReplicas as a workaround while we fix root cause. Also will share repro steps.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job to increase minReplicas for tenant fathom to 3 from 1 at 14:20Z by @Ava (rollback in 30m).
Liam: For root cause, we need to confirm image registry error codes and if token rotation attempted during the spike. I'll pull registry logs and KMS rotation logs.
Raj: Also adding a small change: reduce autoscaler backoff floor for failures from 90s to 30s for dedicated tenants with high SLOs while we investigate. Ops: please approve.
Maya: Thanks. CS will notify customer about temporary minReplicas bump and follow up.
Ava: CS note I'll send: "We're investigating an interaction between a brief billing credential rotation and autoscaler backoff that slowed scale-up. Temporary min replicas increase applied; we're investigating registry retries and will follow up with concrete fixes." :thumbsup:
Raj: I'll open a postmortem ticket with repro steps and propose fixes: 1) clearable failure backoff 2) prefetch/warm-pool improvements 3) better detection of credential rotation vs bad image.
Maya: Perfect. Please add exact repro (traffic pattern + timing) so SRE can try to reproduce in staging.
Liam: copying registry logs to the ticket now.
ops-bot: ticket created: INC-2026-1748 "Fathom Dedicated scale-up lag due to imagepull failures + backoff" assigned to Raj/Liam/Ava
Maya: Good. I'll keep this thread open until we have the PM with root cause and customer response. :grimacing:
